title: Azure Files
description: Use Azure Files to create fully managed file shares that applications can mount like network drives.

data.text: Azure Files provides fully managed cloud file shares that you can access via the industry-standard **SMB** (Server Message Block) protocol or **NFS** (Network File System). This makes it ideal for 'lift-and-shift' scenarios where existing applications expect a file share, and for sharing files between multiple VMs or containers.

You create a file share inside an Azure storage account. Once created, you get a URL and connection string that your app or VM can use to mount the share. Azure Files supports both SMB 3.0 and NFS 4.1.

data.title: Create a File Share with Azure CLI
data.content: Provision a Standard SSD file share named 'shared'
data.code:
az storage account create \
  --name stdemofiles \
  --resource-group rg-demo \
  --location eastus \
  --sku Standard_LRS \
  --kind StorageV2

az storage share-rm create \
  --resource-group rg-demo \
  --storage-account stdemofiles \
  --name shared \
  --quota 100

terms.definition: A fully managed SMB or NFS share in Azure that behaves like a network file server.
Server Message Block, a network file-sharing protocol used by Windows and supported by Azure Files.
Network File System, a protocol commonly used by Linux and Unix systems for file sharing.
A read-only copy of a file share at a point in time, used for backup and recovery.

data.title: Azure File Sync
data.text: For on-premises servers that need local copies of cloud files, Azure File Sync can cache frequently used files on Windows Servers while keeping the authoritative copy in Azure Files.

data.title: Exercise: Mount an Azure File Share
data.description: Create a file share and mount it from a local or VM environment.
steps: Create a storage account with a Standard SSD file share.
Get the storage account key from the Azure Portal.
Mount the share on Linux or Windows using the steps above.
Create a file in the mounted share and confirm it appears in the Azure Portal.
data.expectedOutcome: A mounted file share where you can read and write files from your local OS.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Azure Files provides managed SMB and NFS file shares.
Choose Standard SSD for general use, Premium SSD for high performance.
You can mount shares from Windows, Linux, and cloud services.
Azure File Sync extends cloud shares to on-premises servers.
data.takeaway: Azure Files is the easiest way to add shared file storage to cloud and hybrid applications.
